text: By 2050, many experts believe we will have created Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) — machines that can think, learn, and solve problems as well as a human in any field. The potential benefits are enormous. AGI could find cures for diseases, solve climate change, and automate tedious work, giving us more time for creativity. However, the risks are equally serious. A super-intelligent system could be misused or act in ways we cannot predict, threatening jobs or even safety. While some predict AGI in just a few decades, others say it may take a century or longer. The real challenge is ensuring we build it carefully, with strong ethics, before it becomes too powerful to control.
